issues.failure_explanation: The theorems analyze an exact variational relation over the infinite-dimensional space H_0, using exact characteristic test functions. The implemented methods instead restrict the unknown to a finite-degree DG space and approximate the right-hand side by quadrature or interpolation. No argument transfers existence, stability, or uniqueness to those actual fully discrete algorithms.

failure_location.quote: In this paper, the existence and uniqueness of the numerical solution for CSLDG, as well as the numerical stability of this scheme, are established for the first time

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must formulate the finite-dimensional, quadrature/interpolation-based update actually implemented and prove its solvability and stability, or explicitly restrict all claims to the exact infinite-dimensional relation.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised well-posedness and stability guarantees for CSLDG-A1, CSLDG-A2, and the separated-variable implementation are unsupported by the paper's analysis.
issues.title: The analysis does not cover the implemented fully discrete DG algorithms
issues.why_classification: Preserving the advertised algorithmic guarantees requires a new analysis of different discrete operators; otherwise the central promise must be substantially withdrawn.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \(H_0({\color{blue}{\Omega}})\) becomes a Hilbert space with compact support on the bounded domain

issues.failure_explanation: Functions whose support is compactly contained in an open bounded domain do not form a closed subspace of L^2, so the displayed H_0 is not a Hilbert space. Moreover, support equal to Ω or to an element is not compactly contained there. Multiplication by an element characteristic function therefore does not imply membership in this H_0. For example, with zero velocity and U_0=1 on Ω, the scheme forces U_h^1=1 a.e. on Ω, whose zero extension has support closure Ω and is not in the defined H_0.

failure_location.quote: the sequence \( \{U_h^n(\mathbf{x})\}_{n=0}^{N}\subset H_0(\Omega)\) is called a set of SLDG numerical solutions

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace H_0 by an appropriate closed L^2 space, or by the actual finite-dimensional DG space, and redo all support and Riesz arguments in that space.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical-solution definition excludes ordinary elementwise DG functions, and the membership conclusions used throughout the existence, stability, and uniqueness proofs are false.
issues.title: The compact-support space is not Hilbert and is incompatible with the claimed solutions
issues.why_classification: The defect invalidates the underlying solution space and cannot be fixed while retaining the stated compact-support definition and the claimed class of DG solutions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The vector function \( \mathbf{A}(\mathbf{x},t) = (a_1(\mathbf{x},t), a_2(\mathbf{x},t), \ldots, a_d(\mathbf{x},t))^{\text{T}} \) is assumed to be continuous with respect to both \( \mathbf{x} \) and \( t \), and its first-order partial derivatives are also continuous.
Clearly, the operator \(\operatorname{CODE}_{t_1 \rightarrow t_2}(\cdot)\) is bijective

issues.failure_explanation: Continuous first derivatives give local uniqueness but do not ensure that trajectories exist for every requested time or remain in the domain where A is defined. For instance, dx/dt=x^2 has smooth coefficients but trajectories can blow up in finite time. Thus the upstream domains and characteristic test functions used by the theorem need not exist for an arbitrary T.

failure_location.quote: for any time partition \( T = N \Delta t \) and any spatial partition \( \mathcal{T}_h \), there exists \( U^{n}_h(\mathbf{x}) \in H_0(\Omega) \)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a standard complete-flow hypothesis, such as suitable global Lipschitz and growth bounds together with a compatible boundary extension, and restrict T to the interval on which the flow is a diffeomorphism.
issues.overall_effect: The existence and subsequent stability and uniqueness claims are not established for the full coefficient and time regime stated.
issues.title: Characteristic flow existence and bijectivity are assumed without sufficient hypotheses
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis repairs the construction without changing the method, estimates, or proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Considering the \(L^P\)-norm over the entire space \(\mathbb{R}^d\), the domain of integration remains unchanged as \(\mathbb{R}^d\) before and after the change of variables.
Note that once \(t_1\) and \(t_2\) are fixed, \(\int_{t_1}^{t_2} \mathbf{A}(\mathbf{s}(\tau), \tau) \, \mathrm{d}\tau\) is a constant.

issues.failure_explanation: The characteristic displacement depends on the starting point, so the change of variables has the flow Jacobian, not unit determinant in general. For A(x,t)=x, the flow from t_1 to t_2 is x↦e^{t_2-t_1}x and the pulled-back L^P norm is multiplied by e^{-d(t_2-t_1)/P}. Equality requires a volume-preserving flow, such as div A=0, which is not assumed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the flow Jacobian and derive upper and lower bounds from div A; alternatively add the substantive hypothesis div A=0. The existence and stability proofs must then use the resulting constants.
issues.overall_effect: Both norm-invariance lemmas are false, the boundedness proof for the Riesz functional is invalid as written, and the stability and uniqueness proofs invoke a false equality.
issues.title: Transport by a compressible flow does not preserve L^P norms
issues.why_classification: Comparable boundedness and stability estimates may survive, but they require a nontrivial Jacobian argument and replacement of two central lemmas.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The variable-separation-based dimensional splitting implementation proposed in this paper is applicable to splitting schemes of arbitrary order.

issues.failure_explanation: The Ruth composition contains negative and greater-than-one substeps. Under the paper's separate cumulative x- and y-time clocks, a y-stage advances to t^n+1.3512Δt and another runs backward. Near t=0 or t=T this requires coefficients outside the interval [0,T], where A is not defined. Moreover, no argument is given that the autonomous Ruth coefficients retain fourth order for the explicitly time-dependent split operators and this time scheduling.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must extend the coefficient data to all intermediate times and provide a valid fourth-order nonautonomous splitting construction, or restrict the fourth-order claim to autonomous coefficients.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised arbitrary-order implementation and the stated fourth-order method are not well defined or justified for the paper's general time-dependent transport equation.

issues.failure_explanation: Each directional solve produces values at transverse nodes, and multiplying by the inverse evaluation matrix reconstructs the transverse polynomial coefficients. This is precisely nodal-to-polynomial interpolation, even though it is written as a matrix inversion. Thus the method does not eliminate interpolation in the asserted mathematical sense.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, no interpolation is needed during dimension switching

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Describe the inverse-matrix steps as transverse interpolation or reconstruction and limit the novelty claim to maintaining a two-dimensional modal representation without a separate post-processing stage.
issues.overall_effect: The main claimed distinction from prior interpolation-based dimension switching is materially overstated, although the reconstruction formulas themselves may still define a method.
issues.title: The claimed interpolation-free dimension switching performs interpolation
issues.why_classification: The algorithm can remain intact, but a substantive advertised advantage must be weakened.
